subject: Decision Making
title: Algorithms vs Human Judgment
description: A 60-second lesson on Algorithms vs Human Judgment.

hook.text: A simple algorithm using only three variables outperformed 30 years of experienced parole board judgments on.

buildup.text: Paul Meehl showed in 1954 that statistical models beat clinical judgment in nearly every domain tested.

discovery.text: Humans are inconsistent. The same judge gives different sentences before and after lunch.

twist.text: But algorithms miss context. A domestic violence victim who fought back looks identical to an aggressor in raw data.

climax.text: The best system uses algorithms for consistency and humans for exceptions. Each compensates for the other's blind spots.

punchline.text: Algorithms never have bad days. Humans catch what data cannot. Use both.

quiz.question: Why do simple algorithms often beat expert judgment?
options: Algorithms are perfectly consistent while human judgment varies with mood and fatigue
